summary: SSO assertion audience rotation blocks automated service-account provisioning via infra-broker
description: Automated provisioning jobs that create service accounts via the infra-broker are failing to complete after a recent Okta assertion audience (aud) rotation. The broker validates the SAML/OIDC assertion audience and rejects assertions with the new aud until we update the broker's trust anchors. This started after last week's tenant-wide identity config update.
impact: All automated service-account creation and rotation pipelines that rely on infra-broker SSO assertions are failing in production for the east coast region. Several CI pipelines and internal deployments that require freshly provisioned service identities cannot proceed; estimated 40+ blocked workflows across platform and infra teams.
steps_to_reproduce: Trigger infra-broker create-service-account flow (used by onboarding CI jobs).
Broker requests SSO assertion from Okta with current client_id/audience claim binding.
Okta returns assertion with rotated audience value (post-config change).
Broker validates aud claim against configured allowed audience list and rejects the assertion with 401/invalid_audience.
Provisioning job logs 'invalid audience' and aborts; no account created.
logs: 2026-03-12T08:12:03Z infra-broker ERROR auth: assertion rejected: invalid_audience: expected 'urn:redwood:infra-broker:v1' or 'urn:redwood:infra-broker:v1:legacy' but got 'urn:redwood:infra-broker:v2'
Okta audit entry 2026-03-12T08:11:58Z: Application 'infra-broker' assertion audience updated via admin console by identity-admins@redwood.com
CI job ci/onboard-service#472 failed: provisioning aborted (exit 1) — see infra-broker logs above.
investigation_notes: Triage: confirmed failures correlate with Okta audience change rolled 2026-03-11 23:00 UTC. Multiple infra-broker instances show identical rejection error.
Hypothesis: infra-broker enforces a strict aud whitelist and was not configured to accept the new v2 audience value used by Okta after org-wide audience normalization.
Checked infra-broker config in vault: allowed_audiences currently contains only v1 values (urn:redwood:infra-broker:v1, urn:redwood:infra-broker:v1:legacy).

Okta change request PR ID: IDP-9876 (identity-admins) shows planned audience canonicalization; change went to prod without a downstream config update ticket. Linked slack thread #idp-change 2026-03-11.
Temporary test: adding v2 to allowed_audiences on a staging broker allowed assertions to validate; provisioning completed successfully in staging.
comments: Aisha Khan (Reporter) 2026-03-12: Observed immediate spike in provisioning failures after the IdP change window. Opening ticket so identity and infra teams can coordinate a safe rollback or config update.

Ethan Li (Assignee) 2026-03-12: Reproduced on staging once we simulated the new aud claim. Adding this to infra-broker's allowed audiences in staging works. Will coordinate change in prod with Security review.

Marta Ruiz (Identity Team) 2026-03-12: The audience normalization was scheduled; we missed notifying downstream owners for infra-broker. We can push a short-lived alias (v1->v2) on the IdP but need infra approval for a config change window.

SRE Oncall (2026-03-13): Recommended hotfix path: add 'urn:redwood:infra-broker:v2' to infra-broker allowed_audiences via vault rotation, then rotate back once downstream rollout completes. Noted need for coordinated change window to avoid token reuse issues.
Security (2026-03-13): Caution: adding additional accepted audience widens token acceptance surface; prefer IdP to emit both aud values for a short transitional window if possible.
resolution: Workaround applied: infra-broker allowed_audiences was updated in Vault to include the new v2 audience, and the change was deployed to all prod infra-broker replicas at 2026-03-14T02:05Z. Provisioning resumed.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-14T02:12Z: infra-broker rolling restart completed across us-east cluster; health checks passed.
Post-fix validation: 47 previously failing onboarding CI jobs retried successfully; no further invalid_audience errors observed after fix.

Follow-up actions: (1) Identity team to coordinate future audience rotations with downstream owners; (2) Add automated integration test to catch aud whitelist mismatches during IdP change windows (ticket created INT-201349); (3) Update runbook with emergency rollback and dual-audience transition pattern.
